task: Establish package build/check work counters on the Phase 26.1 baseline.
observation: The compiler-perf M1 harness showed each current margo build checks every package in the graph (4/4 packages and 4/4 modules in the four-package chain), while moss check on one edited package invoked one checker package. The existing margo CLI rejects build --check, so the baseline records that unsupported mode and profiles margo build as its full-work fallback.
impact: Package graph and edit/revert scenarios can now report actual package invocations and checker work before implementing interface freshness, skip, or checkstop behavior.

resolution.summary: M1 baseline is established; subsequent workstreams should compare counters against these rows and preserve the command-mode distinction.

tool_used: Margo, moss --check profiling, and compiler-perf M1 suite

task: Expand the M1 package counter harness into a future incremental-build gate.
observation: Recording the R-rule target beside observed package counts exposed an invalid E3 fixture: the original edited signature was not forwarded through dependents, so a full-graph target would have been unjustified. Forwarding explicit-result changes through chain, fan-out, and generic fixtures made the target test meaningful. Moving the package work scenarios to make package-perf also keeps compiler-perf focused on timing.
impact: The same measurement table now acts as a truthful pre-G1 baseline and can become a hard target gate after G1, while avoiding unrelated timing-suite failures.

resolution.summary: R-rule targets are explicit, E3 propagation fixtures are connected, and M1 runs independently from compiler timing.

tool_used: make package-perf and M1 work-counter report
